drhp.business: Incorporated in 1993 in Bangalore, the Company manufactures hard gelatin capsules, HPMC vegetarian capsules and a range of specialty and regulatory capsule variants, supplied to pharmaceutical and nutraceutical customers in India and abroad from facilities at Bangalore and Puducherry. Through its subsidiary Natural Biogenex Private Limited it operates a greenfield facility at Tumkur that manufactures complex steroidal active pharmaceutical ingredients using fermentation-based synthesis from key starting materials, a vertical that reached commercial production during FY26. drhp.expansion: FY26 completed a multi-year build-out across three units and two businesses. In the capsule business the Company commissioned a new HPMC line for double-zero capsules during the year, taking installed capsule capacity to 20.25 BCPA as on 31 March 2026, and continued to invest in next-generation hard-capsule manufacturing equipment that raises output, adds automation with lower per-unit labour cost, improves energy efficiency and shortens production cycles. risks.note: A licensing matter at the Puducherry capsule facility led to a temporary shutdown that disrupted production and dispatches for part of FY26 and was the principal drag on volumes. The licence position was resolved during the year, but the episode shows how a single permission issue at one of only three units can interrupt output while fixed costs continue.
risks.risk: Site licensing and regulatory permission risk at manufacturing facilities

risks.note: Management identifies the supply and cost of raw materials such as gelatin and HPMC, which are often imported and subject to price movement, as an enduring challenge that can affect production costs and margins.
risks.risk: Raw-material cost and availability, particularly gelatin and HPMC

risks.note: An estimated 65% to 70% of key intermediates for the Indian API industry are still sourced from China, exposing the sector to supply-chain and price risk. This is the very dependence the Company's backward integration is designed to reduce, but the starting-material chain remains a structural exposure.
risks.risk: Import dependence for key starting materials and intermediates

risks.note: The API business, in its first year of commercial production, operated against global pricing pressure while establishing customer connections, and the market is marked by geographic concentration and a shift in competition towards complex, higher-value molecules.
risks.risk: Pricing pressure and competition in the global API market

risks.note: The full-year cost of depreciation and finance charges on newly commissioned capacity arrived at a stage when revenue from the newer platforms was still building. Returns depend on restoring and lifting utilisation across the capsule sites and building volumes in the API business.
risks.risk: Execution and ramp-up risk on newly commissioned capacity

risks.note: The Tumkur facility is still working towards regulatory certification; until it is obtained, access to regulated export markets - and therefore the facility's addressable market - remains limited. Global authorities are also intensifying inspection of manufacturing sites and enforcing environmental and quality standards.
risks.risk: Pending regulatory certification for the API facility

risks.note: Commissioning the API facility extended the control environment to an operation with its own requirements for process safety, quality documentation and environmental compliance; bringing it within the established framework of authorisation, review and audit remains a focus as the facility scales.
risks.risk: Extension of the control environment to a second, more complex manufacturing operation

risks.note: The Company has given corporate guarantees to its subsidiary Natural Biogenex Private Limited under section 186 of the Companies Act, 2013, so the parent carries contingent exposure to the performance of the API business.
risks.risk: Contingent exposure to the subsidiary through corporate guarantees
